work.title: Accensa
work.description: The merchant back-office for x402 sellers on Stellar. I work across all three public repositories: the Next.js dashboard with its event indexer and SDK, the Soroban contracts that anchor payment receipts and hold the refund vault, and the facilitator that settles x402 payment requests. Receipt verification is public, so a buyer never has to trust the merchant's own database.
work.frontend: The part a merchant actually touches is accensa-app: a Next.js and TypeScript dashboard, with the public receipt verifier at its /verify route reading anchored state off the chain rather than out of a database.

shots.alt: Accensa landing page: trustless payments for AI agents, with buttons to verify a receipt and open the dashboard.
Accensa integration section showing a verifyReceipt call imported from the SDK and checked against an anchored root.

work.title: StaffPurse
work.description: Spend records anchored on Soroban, with a public verification dashboard so an employer can check a disbursement without trusting the payroll system that produced it. Merged work lands in three repositories: staffpurse-web, the public dashboard, plus staffpurse-app and staffpurse-contracts.

work.title: Tollcraft
work.description: Rust tooling for Soroban developers who find out about compute cost too late. soroban-cost-linter flags resource-expensive contract patterns at write time, soroban-budget-assert adds runtime budget assertions, and soroban-cost-profiler explains a failed budget by showing where the instructions actually went.
work.frontend: Tollcraft/docs is the front end for the same three crates: a VitePress site in Vue with a custom theme, so the pipeline reads as one product rather than three command line tools.

shots.alt: Tollcraft site landing page: stop guessing your gas bill, a three-tier cost pipeline for Stellar smart contracts.
Tollcraft pipeline section: three cards for Cost Linter, Budget Assert and Cost Profiler, each linking to its repository.

work.title: Airlock
work.description: A supply-chain scanner for Stellar and Soroban repositories. Python 3.11, standard library only, shipped as a CLI and a composite GitHub Action. Its rules judge a change against the policy that existed before the change, and it fails closed on every file it did not read.

experience.detail: Backend services in Go, with AI-assisted tooling carrying the boilerplate. File system and configuration work on Linux hosts, and pairing through technical sprints to debug Go applications and shorten the review loop.

Recurring reporting in Excel, Power BI, Power Apps and Power Automate, and dataset reviews that found discrepancies upstream of the decisions made from them. This is where the habit of checking a number before publishing it came from.
